t: Barcelona grew from an Iberian settlement into the Roman colony of Barcino, served as a royal seat of the Visigoths, and from 801 was the seat of the Counts of Barcelona, who became kings of the Crown of Aragon through a marriage in 1137.

After the Catalan institutions took the Habsburg side in the War of the Spanish Succession, its separate status was abolished in 1716, but the port, industry and the Eixample, laid out from the 1850s, made it one of the richest cities of Spain.
It was Republican in the Spanish Civil War, was bombed in March 1938 and fell on 26 January 1939, and under Franco the institutions of Catalonia were abolished; autonomy was restored in 1977.
dyk: On 16 March 1794, although France and Spain were at war, the French astronomer Pierre François André Méchain was allowed into the fortress of Montjuïc to make observations used to measure the distance from Dunkirk to Barcelona, the basis of the first prototype metre.
ev: The Romans redraw the town as the colony of Barcino
The Visigothic king Ataulf holds his court at Barcino and is murdered there
Louis the Pious, son of Charlemagne, captures Barcelona after a siege of several months
The army of Almanzor sacks the city
Alfonso II becomes both Count of Barcelona and King of Aragon, following the marriage of 1137
The city falls after a siege and assault in the War of the Spanish Succession
Air raids from 16 to 18 March kill more than 1,000 people
More than a million people demonstrate for the restoration of Catalan autonomy, which is granted within a month

f.founded: Settlement on the site is older than 5000 BCE; the Laietani, an Iberian people, held Barkeno in the 3rd and 2nd centuries BCE, and the Romans redrew the town as a castrum about 15 BCE. Founding by Hamilcar Barca or by Hercules is legend.
f.where: On a coastal plain about 5 km wide on the Mediterranean in north-eastern Spain, between the Collserola range and the sea, and between the Llobregat river to the south-west and the Besòs river to the north.
f.known: The Roman colony of Barcino; a Visigothic royal seat; the County of Barcelona and the Crown of Aragon; a medieval trading port with a large Jewish community; the 1714 siege; the Eixample; Gaudí and Catalan modernisme; the Spanish Civil War; the Olympic Games of 1992
f.today: Barcelona is the capital of the autonomous community of Catalonia and the second largest city of Spain.
